about.text: A Lighthouse called Kanata is a contemporary art gallery in the Jingumae area of Shibuya-ku, Tokyo, near Omotesando Station. It was established in 2007 by Wahei Aoyama with the aim of introducing contemporary Japanese art and aesthetics to an international audience. The gallery's program centers on sculpture and painting by artists working within an emerging strand of Japanese aesthetics that reinstates beauty, technique, and materiality as central concerns, spanning media such as ceramics, glass, lacquer, metal, bamboo and wood alongside painting. The gallery frames its mission around a 'Return to Innocence' in contemporary art practice, positioning its roster of artists, many working in traditional craft mediums, within a global contemporary art context.

about.text: Tomio Koyama Gallery opened in 1996 in Saga-cho, Koto-ku, Tokyo, and has since become a key platform for Japanese contemporary art. From its earliest years the gallery took part in international art fairs and served as an early point of introduction for young Japanese artists, helping shape a broader current within the country's contemporary art scene. It now operates spaces in Roppongi, Tennoz, Maebashi, and, since November 2024, Kyobashi. The program spans generations and media, representing figures such as Kishio Suga, Hiroshi Sugito, Mika Ninagawa, and Richard Tuttle alongside exhibitions of ceramic artists, reflecting an approach that moves freely across nationality and genre.

about.text: Gallery Tsubaki is a contemporary art gallery in the Kyobashi district of Tokyo, near Ginza. According to the gallery's own diary, its director left his father's gallery, Tsubaki Kindai Garou, to open Gallery Tsubaki around 1984. Since then it has built a program centered on Japanese artists working across painting, sculpture, ceramics, woodblock printmaking and photography, with a particular fondness for surreal, fantastical and meticulously crafted imagery. The gallery represents a large roster of emerging and mid-career Japanese artists, several of whom it has shown continuously for decades, and it regularly places their work in international art fairs across Taipei, Seoul, Busan and beyond, positioning itself as an advocate for Japanese contemporary art in the wider Asian market.

about.text: Kaikai Kiki Gallery occupies the basement of an office building in Motoazabu, Tokyo, that once served as the private viewing room for Kaikai Kiki's headquarters. The space was reopened as a public gallery in March 2008, after Kaikai Kiki relocated from a prefab studio in Saitama's Asaka city to Tokyo in 2006. The gallery presents exhibitions of its own roster of Kaikai Kiki artists alongside international figures such as Mark Grotjahn, Matthew Monahan, Seonna Hong and Friedrich Kunath, aiming to build connections between Japanese and international contemporary art. Its stated goal is to manage artists and sell work in a way that gives art new social value, continuing to invite artists from both Japan and abroad to exhibit in its roughly 197 square meter exhibition space.

about.text: KOMIYAMA TOKYO G is a gallery space in Tokyo's Kanda-Jimbocho book district, launched in 2022 by the century-old secondhand bookstore Komiyama Shoten. It presents solo exhibitions and group shows spanning photography, illustration, ceramics, tattoo art, fashion and fetish culture, often mixing the bookstore's archival material with contemporary artists' work. Throughout the year it also hosts art book fairs and publication-related exhibitions tied to photobooks and artist monographs. The program favors emerging and cult-following artists working in painting, ceramics, digital/CG art, airbrush illustration, and documentary photography, reflecting the eclectic subcultural interests of its bookstore origins.

about.text: Misa Shin Gallery opened in November 2010 in Shirokane, Tokyo, in a former ironworks building, and relocated in August 2018 to Minamiazabu, a quiet residential district near several embassies. The gallery presents exhibitions of Japanese and international artists working with a conceptual approach, giving particular attention to mid-career artists and to Japanese conceptualism of the 1960s and 1970s, aiming to reassess this postwar history for international audiences. Beyond its exhibition program, the gallery advises corporate art collections and art programs in Japan and has been involved in public art projects in Zhengzhou, China, and Doha, Qatar. It also explores connections between art and other disciplines such as architecture, theater and music.

about.text: Mizuma Art Gallery was founded in Tokyo in 1994 by executive director Mizuma Sueo. The gallery introduces Japanese and Asian artists with distinctive, style-independent sensibilities to the international art scene. As contemporary art markets in Asia expanded, Mizuma opened a Beijing space in 2008 and a Singapore gallery at Gillman Barracks in 2012, followed by an artist residence, Rumah Kijang Mizuma, in Yogyakarta in 2014 to foster exchange between Japanese and Indonesian artists. The gallery is known for active participation in major international fairs such as Art Basel Hong Kong and The Armory Show, and for producing artists who have gone on to international careers.

about.text: Mizuma Art Gallery was founded in Tokyo in 1994 by Executive Director Sueo Mizuma. Since then it has built a program centered on Japanese and, increasingly, Southeast and East Asian artists whose work resists passing stylistic trends. The gallery expanded internationally, opening Mizuma Gallery in Singapore's Gillman Barracks in 2012, running the Rumah Kijang Mizuma residency in Yogyakarta from 2014 to 2019, and operating Mizuma & Kips in New York with Kips Gallery from 2018 to 2023. It regularly takes part in major international fairs such as Art Basel Hong Kong, Art Dubai and Art Taipei. In 2024 the gallery marked its thirtieth anniversary as a longstanding platform for contemporary art from diverse Asian backgrounds.

about.text: Ota Fine Arts was founded in 1994 in Tokyo, initially in the Ebisu area, and has long positioned itself as a pioneer of Japanese contemporary art, notably giving early support to Yayoi Kusama. The gallery moved to Roppongi in 2003, relocated to the Tokyo bay area, and returned to a renewed Roppongi space in 2011. It later opened a nearby viewing room, 7CHOME, near the National Art Center. The gallery expanded internationally with a Singapore space at Gillman Barracks in 2012 and a Shanghai gallery in 2017, which reopened in the Rockbund district in 2023. Ota Fine Arts represents artists working in painting, video, craft and installation, with a program emphasizing dialogue among East and Southeast Asian, and more recently Middle Eastern, artists.

about.text: Pace Gallery is a global contemporary art gallery founded in Boston in 1960 by Arne Glimcher, now led by CEO Marc Glimcher and President Samanthe Rubell. The gallery operates spaces in New York, Los Angeles, London, Geneva, Berlin, Seoul, and Tokyo, with offices in Beijing and Hong Kong. about.text: space Un is a Tokyo arts and culture venue focused on contemporary African art and cultural exchange between Japan and Africa. It was initiated by collector Edna Dumas, driven by her passion for contemporary African art and wish to support African artists, and co-founded with actor and artist Yuta Nakano. The gallery presents exhibitions of artists from the African continent and its diaspora, alongside cross-disciplinary programming including workshops, music events, film nights, and lectures. It also runs an invitation-only residency program linking artists' stays at Yoshino Cedar House in Nara with solo exhibitions in Tokyo. The gallery space in Minami-Aoyama was designed by architect Go Hasegawa, blending Japanese spatial sensibility with African heritage.

TSCA regularly mounts solo and group exhibitions in its Tokyo space and participates in major international art fairs, presenting its artists' work in dialogue with wider contemporary art discourse. about.text: Tokyo Gallery + BTAP is Japan's oldest contemporary art gallery, founded in Tokyo in 1950 by Yamamoto Takashi together with Shimizu Kusuo, initially as the Sukiyabashi Gallery. From the late 1950s it introduced Western abstraction, Gutai, Neo Dada and Mono-ha artists, later becoming a key champion of postwar Korean and Chinese contemporary art. In 2002 it opened BTAP in Beijing's 798 Art Zone, and in 2006 adopted its current dual name. Led today by Yamamoto Toyotsugu in Tokyo and Tabata Yukito in Beijing, the gallery continues to present postwar Japanese art alongside younger generations of artists across Japan, Korea and China, and takes part regularly in international art fairs.

about.text: Tomio Koyama Gallery is a Tokyo contemporary art gallery founded in 1996 in Saga-cho, Koto-ku, by Tomio Koyama. It has since expanded to multiple spaces across the city, currently operating in Roppongi, Tennoz and Kyobashi (opened 2024), as well as a space in Maebashi. about.text: YUKI-SIS is a contemporary art gallery in Tokyo's Nihombashi Kayabacho district, currently directed by Yuki Terajima. The gallery's name blends the director's own name with the Egyptian goddess Isis. Before settling in Kayabacho in 2023, the gallery operated in other Tokyo neighborhoods linked by the word "bridge" (hashi), including Asakusabashi and near Nihombashi Mitsukoshimae. Its current space, on the second floor of the Koura Dai-Ichi Building overlooking a river and bridge leading to Tokyo Bay, sits among several other galleries in the same building. YUKI-SIS presents a program spanning painting, photography, printmaking, sculpture, and animation, and participates in art fairs such as Art Fair Tokyo.

about.text: YUKIKOMIZUTANI is a contemporary art gallery in Tokyo, founded in 2021 with the aim of bringing contemporary art from Tokyo to an international audience. The gallery is based inside TERRADA ART COMPLEX in Tennozu, an area where the Meguro River meets Tokyo Bay, home to the largest concentration of galleries in Japan. Through its exhibition program, YUKIKOMIZUTANI supports a diverse roster of artists working across painting, sculpture, textile and installation, and takes part in major art fairs in Japan and abroad. The gallery describes its mission as elevating the role of art in contemporary culture while helping develop Tennozu Isle into a significant arts and culture hub.

about.text: Yutaka Kikutake Gallery opened in Roppongi, Tokyo, in 2015, later adding a second space in Kyobashi in 2024. The gallery presents exhibitions of international and domestic artists, supporting their practices and seeking opportunities to present their work internationally. Grounded in a strong sense of recent art history, the program explores newly created forms of expression and emphasizes art's contribution to society. Beyond exhibitions, the gallery runs workshops for all ages and publishes artist books alongside the lifestyle and culture magazine Chic and the art criticism journal Kyoku. The Kyobashi space focuses on group exhibitions reflecting the gallery's core values.
